author: summonjikon

title: It should be “so that I can be”
body: I don’t like the phrasing “so that I can become”. For some habits that I want to add, I already view myself as having that identity, and I just want to have the path as the goal. “So that I can become” always feels like chasing something in the future. The moment I start a habit of reading, I am *already* a reader. Then if you force me to use this future phrasing, it just makes me feel like I’m not yet the type of person that I want to be. At least give the option to change it.

author: sffortytwo

title: How much is enough?
body:
James Clear’s book was not the first great habit book but I think it was the best. Good for him that he sold 15 million copies. James’ app is late to the habit tracking game, but it looks like the best habit app that I have ever seen. Just like the book it can benefit millions of people, and with the audience he already has, it will surely be very successful. 

 But why this excessive price of €130/year, €20/month?! This amount is definitely too expensive for the majority of people that would benefit from this app. Investing in good habits and in a good app is a good cause, but this pricepoint is clearly only optimized for investing in James’ personal luxury habits. 🥂🤑 This one star rating is my protest!

author: Robbie JS

title: Seriously?
body:
The app looks quite nice but you can only track one habit without upgrading to Pro (which is not cheap), where you can track 3. This is useless for me, I have more than 3 habits to track before I have breakfast. Meditation, cold shower, brain training and gym for starters. 
I uninstalled it after realising I can’t even track my daily habits, let alone weekly ones. Really missed the ball on this one, hopefully the developers pivot quickly and make some changes.
